healthcareSystem: Universal (Croatian Health Insurance Fund — HZZO). EU citizens covered by EHIC. All others pay out-of-pocket or via travel insurance.
qualityNotes: Good quality healthcare, especially in Zagreb, Split, and coastal tourist areas. Major cities have modern hospitals. English is commonly spoken in tourist areas and hospitals. Rural areas may have fewer English-speaking doctors. Pharmacies are widely available.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open Mon-Fri 8am-8pm, Sat 8am-3pm. Some 24/7 pharmacies in Zagreb and major cities. Look for 'Ljekarna' signs. Tourist areas often have pharmacies with extended hours during summer.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacists in tourist areas often speak English and German. Many common OTC medications are available. EU prescriptions are accepted. The Croatian pharmacy system is well-developed — look for the green cross sign.
prescriptionRules: EU prescriptions are accepted. Prescriptions from outside the EU may need verification from a local doctor. Croatia has adopted EU pharmaceutical standards. Some medications more freely available than in some other EU countries.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substance. Requires prescription or doctor approval. Small quantities for personal use may be brought with documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription or doctor consultation in Croatia. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. EU regulations apply. Carry doctor's letter and original prescription. Customs may inspect quantities.

restrictedMeds.name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin) and ADHD medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires documentation. Contact Croatian health authorities or your embassy if you need to bring ADHD medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal for recreational use and strictly controlled medically. CBD products with zero THC are legal. Do not bring any THC-containing products.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in Croatian or English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. EU citizens should carry EHIC. Non-EU travelers should carry prescriptions and a multilingual medical certificate.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not legally required for tourists, but strongly recommended.
travelInsurance.tips: Croatia is affordable for healthcare compared to Western Europe, but travel insurance is still essential for emergencies and medical evacuation. EHIC covers EU citizens for emergency care at public facilities. Summer travelers should note that island hospitals are limited — air evacuation may be needed for serious conditions.

recommended: tick-borne encephalitis (if hiking in inland forested areas)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Croatia has had sporadic tick-borne encephalitis cases in forested inland regions. Standard precautions for outdoor activities apply.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Croatia. Croatian tap water is tested regularly and meets EU standards. Bottled water is widely available.
foodSafetyTips: Croatia has good food safety standards. Coastal seafood ( Adriatic fish, shellfish) is generally safe at reputable restaurants. Traditional dishes like pašticada, truffles (Istria), and fresh seafood are highlights. Be cautious with unfamiliar wild plants or mushrooms.
medicalTourismNote: Croatia is known for health and wellness tourism — spa resorts on the Adriatic coast, health retreats, and dental tourism. Costs are significantly lower than Western Europe while quality is good.
metaDescription: Health & medication guide for Croatia. Emergency numbers (112/194/192/193), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, travel insurance, and vaccination recommendations for travelers.

hospitals.name: KBC Split
hospitals.notes: Major hospital serving Split and the Dalmatian coast.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care. Croatia is a popular dental tourism destination.
dentalCare.notes: Zagreb and coastal cities have dental clinics catering to tourists. Prices 50-60% lower than Western Europe.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hospital emergency departments handle dental emergencies.

mentalHealth.notes: English mental health services mainly in Zagreb.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Croatia's accessibility is limited in historic areas. Dubrovnik's Old Town has many steps.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Zagreb trams are partially accessible. Ferries to islands have basic accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Dubrovnik's Old Town is extremely challenging for wheelchairs — steep limestone streets with many steps. Split's waterfront is more manageable.

insuranceClaimProcess: EU citizens with EHIC access public healthcare. Keep receipts and medical documentation. Tourist areas have doctors used to treating international patients.
